questions.question: What is the official language of Bhutan, a neighbouring country of India?
questions.questionHtml: What is the official language of Bhutan, a neighbouring country of India?
questions.solution: The official language of Bhutan, a neighbouring country of India, is Dzongkha. It is a South Tibetan language spoken by over half a million people in Bhutan. The language is also used in government administration, education, and media.

questions.question: Zoroaster was a/an ______ prophet.
questions.questionHtml: Zoroaster was a/an ______ prophet.
questions.solution: Zoroaster was an ancient Iranian spiritual leader who founded Zoroastrianism. The religion was a major one in Iran for over a thousand years, with some Zoroastrians migrating to India and becoming the ancestors of today's Parsis. The basic teachings of Zoroaster are "Good thoughts, Good Words, and Good Deeds". The Avesta is the sacred book of Zoroastrianism, similar to the Vedas. Option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question: 'Avesta’, also called ‘Zend-Avesta’, is the sacred book of:
questions.questionHtml: 'Avesta’, also called ‘Zend-Avesta’, is the sacred book of:
questions.solution: 'Avesta’, also called ‘Zend-Avesta’, is the sacred book of Zoroastrianism. It contains the basic teachings of Zoraster known as the Gatha. A fire temple in Zoroastrianism is the place of worship for Zoroastrians, usually called Dar-e-Mehr. In the Zoroastrian religion, fire, together with clean water, are agents of ritual purity.

questions.question: Which of the following monuments is also known as the ‘Taj of the Deccan’?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following monuments is also known as the ‘Taj of the Deccan’?
questions.solution: The question identifies the monument called the 'Taj of the Deccan'. Bibi ka Maqbara, located in Aurangabad, Maharashtra, is a mausoleum built by Prince Azam Shah in memory of his mother, Dilras Banu Begum. Constructed between 1651-1661, it resembles the Taj Mahal. Other options include Qutub Minar, Chand Minar, and Mahabat Maqbara.

questions.question: Which ancient text, attributed to the sage Vyasa, is a central epic of ancient India and consists of 100,000 verses in 18 parvas (books)?
questions.questionHtml: Which ancient text, attributed to the sage Vyasa, is a central epic of ancient India and consists of 100,000 verses in 18 parvas (books)?
questions.solution: The Mahabharata, attributed to the sage Vyasa, is a central epic of ancient India consisting of over 100,000 verses in 18 parvas (books). Originally known as the Jaya Samhita, it had 8,800 verses and focused on the Kurukshetra War. Vyasa's disciple Vaisampayana expanded it to 15,200 verses, calling it the Bharata. Over centuries, it grew to its current size. The epic, whose name means "Collection of Victories," highlights the Pandavas' victory over the Kauravas. The Mahabharata is one of the world's longest epics and a significant part of Hindu culture, retold for centuries.

questions.question: Under the influence of the Greeks, which of the following art styles flourished in India?
questions.questionHtml: Under the influence of the Greeks, which of the following art styles flourished in India?
questions.solution: Under Greek influence, the Gandhar art style emerged in India, blending Indian and Greek elements. Flourishing between the 1st and 5th centuries CE, it introduced iconic Buddha sculptures, symbolizing Buddhism. Notable for intricate carvings, realistic figures, and architectural Greek motifs, it spread widely across Asia through the Silk Road.

questions.question: Marathi language is in the _______ language family.
questions.questionHtml: Marathi language is in the _______ language family.
questions.solution: Marathi belongs to the Indo Aryan language family, a major branch of the Indo-European languages. It is one of India's 22 scheduled languages and the official language of Maharashtra. Other Indo Aryan languages include Hindi, Bengali, Gujarati, Punjabi, and Urdu. Marathi has a rich literary tradition spanning over a thousand years and is written in the Devanagari script. Influenced by various historical and cultural factors, including the Maratha Empire, Marathi is spoken by over 83 million people worldwide.

questions.question: The 14 th Dalai Lama resides in _______.
questions.questionHtml: The 14<sup>th</sup> Dalai Lama resides in _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3 i.e., Dharamsala

  • The 14th Dalai Lama resides in Dharamsala.
  • Tenzin Gyatso is the 14th Dalai Lama.
  • He is the spiritual leader of Tibet. 
  • He was born on 6 July 1935, to a farming family, in a small village of Taktser, Amdo, north-eastern Tibet. 
  • In 1959, Chinese troops suppressed the Tibetan national uprising in Lhasa.
  • Following that, the Dalai Lama was forced to escape to India into exile. 
  • Since then he has been living in Dharamsala, India.
  • The Dalai Lamas are believed to be the manifestations of Avalokiteshvara or Chenrezig, by Tibetan Buddhists.
  • Chenrezig or Avalokiteshvara is the Bodhisattva of Compassion and the patron saint of Tibet. 
  • Bodhisattvas are enlightened beings, who are on the path to becoming a Buddha, and have vowed to be reborn in the world to help all living beings

questions.question: Pattachitra art form is dedicated to which Lord in Hindu mythology?
questions.questionHtml: Pattachitra art form is dedicated to which Lord in Hindu mythology?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lord Jagannath.

Key Points

  • Pattachitra art has been majorly inspired by the Lord Jagannath who is considered as the incarnation of Lord Krishna.
  • It is a general term for traditional cloth-based scroll painting, based in the eastern states of India like Odisha and West Bengal.
  • It is known for its intricate details as well as mythological narratives and folktales inscribed in it.

Additional Information

  • This art form originated as early as the 12th century.
  • The name Pattachitra is taken from the Sanskrit language word 'patta', refers to "cloth" and 'chitra', refers to "the picture".
  • Its style is a mix of both folk and classical elements with more inclination towards folk forms.

questions.question: Which among the following is NOT a component of Lion Capital at Sarnath, India?
questions.questionHtml: Which among the following is NOT a component of Lion Capital at Sarnath, India?
questions.solution: The Lion Capital at Sarnath, India, built by Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE, features four lions, Dharma Chakras, a lotus base, and a bell-shaped inverted lotus. questions.question: In which of the following regions of India is the Mundari language spoken?

questions.solution: The Chota Nagpur Plateau, located in eastern India and spanning parts of Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal, and Bihar, is known for its rich cultural and geographical diversity. It is home to the Munda people, primary speakers of the Mundari language, as well as other indigenous tribes like the Santals and Oraons. The plateau is characterized by vast forests, rich mineral deposits, and hilly terrain, including districts such as Ranchi, Gumla, and Khunti. In contrast, regions like the Malwa Plateau, Thar Desert, and Baghelkhand have different linguistic demographics, with languages such as Hindi, Malvi, Rajasthani, Marwari, and Bagheli predominating.

  • The Jadupatua paintings of the Santhal tribes are vertical scroll paintings that were performed on cloth in earlier days but later these paintings were done on papers.
  • The scrolls were made up of sheets of paper that were either glued together or sewn together and a piece of old cloth or calico was sewn to the end of the scroll to protect the paper from damage.
  • The stories in paintings are depicted in a series of simple clear-cut images in panels divided by horizontal bands.
  • Seven themes of the scroll paintings made by jadupatuas in the Santal Parganas are :
    • Life in Death’s kingdom
    • The story of the creation of the Santals as preserved in Santal tradition
    • The Santal festival of Bahajatras
    • Mass meetings of the Santals for dance
    • The personification of Santal clans
    • A tiger or leopard often with a human rider
    • Finally, the adventures of Krishna with the milkmaid.
  • Other folk paintings of Jharkhand-Paitkar, Jadopatia Paintings, Sohrai Art, Kohver Art, Ganju Art, Kurmi Art, Mundas Art, Turi art, Ghatwal art.

questions.question: With reference of Ajivikas, consider the following statements. a) Makkhali Gosala was the prominent teacher of this sect. b) Ajivikas believed in fatalism. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.questionHtml:
With reference of Ajivikas, consider the following statements.
a) Makkhali Gosala was the prominent teacher of this sect.
b) Ajivikas believed in fatalism.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both a and b.

Key Points

  • Makkhali Gosala was indeed the prominent teacher of the Ajivika sect, which is a fundamental point in understanding the history of this ascetic sect.
  • The Ajivikas were known for their belief in fatalism, the idea that all events are predetermined and therefore inevitable.
  • The sect was a contemporary of Buddhism and Jainism and had a significant influence during the time of the Mauryan Empire.
  • Ajivikas followed a strict ascetic lifestyle and believed in the concept of niyati (destiny).

Additional Information

  • Ajivikas:
    • The Ajivikas were an ascetic sect that emerged in ancient India around the same time as Buddhism and Jainism. They believed in the doctrine of predetermination, where every event is preordained and humans are powerless to change their destiny.
    • Makkhali Gosala: He was one of the key figures in the Ajivika sect. His teachings emphasized the power of fate over individual effort.
    • The teachings of the Ajivikas were based on the principle of niyati, which means destiny. This doctrine suggested that everything in the world was predetermined and fixed, and human efforts to change their fate were futile.
    • The Ajivikas practiced extreme asceticism and renunciation, similar to other contemporary religious movements like Jainism.
  • Fatalism:
    • Fatalism is the philosophical doctrine suggesting that all events are predetermined and inevitable, a belief that is central to the Ajivika philosophy.
    • It implies that human actions have no effect on the future, which is already decided by destiny or fate.
    • This belief can lead to a deterministic outlook on life, where individuals accept whatever happens without trying to change their circumstances.
    • In the context of Ajivikas, this meant that their ascetic practices were part of adhering to their predetermined path.

questions.question: which of the following materials were pillars in Stupas built during Ashoka’s reign?
questions.questionHtml: which of the following materials were pillars in Stupas built during Ashoka’s reign?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is StoneKey Points

  • The pillars in stupas built during Ashoka’s reign were primarily made of stone.
  • Ashoka's reign (circa 268–232 BCE) is known for the construction of numerous stupas and pillars as part of his efforts to spread Buddhism across India.
  • The Ashokan pillars were made of polished sandstone, not granite or marble.
  • These pillars often featured inscriptions detailing Ashoka's edicts and policies, which were written in Prakrit and other languages.
  • Bricks were used in the construction of the stupa structures, but the pillars themselves were carved out of stone, particularly sandstone.
  • These pillars are iconic symbols of Ashoka’s commitment to Buddhist teachings and his role in the spread of the religion.
  • The most famous Ashokan pillar is the Lion Capital at Sarnath, which is also the national emblem of India.

questions.question: Ganesh Chaturthi is observed in ________ month of Hindu calendar.

questions.solution: In Hinduism, Ganesh Chaturthi is a ten-day celebration commemorating the birth of the elephant-headed god Ganesha, who is known as the knowledge and prosperity god. The Sanskrit philosopher Kanada Kashyapa (2nd–3rd century) expounded its theories and is credited with founding the school.

questions.question: Ramabhar Stupa, which marks the site where Lord Buddha was cremated, is situated in which state of India?

questions.question: What is the State religion of Maldives?

questions.solution: The state religion of the Maldives is Islam. The 2008 Constitution mandates Sunni Islam as the official religion, and citizenship is tied to adherence to Islam. Promoting other religions is illegal, with strict penalties for violations.

questions.question: To which state does the Bagh style of textile art printing belong?
questions.questionHtml: To which state does the Bagh style of textile art printing belong?

  • Bagh gets its name from the ancient Bagheshwari Devi temple situated there and is famous both for the ancient Bagh Caves.
  • The process of printing and fabric treatment is a multi-layered process that includes colour treatment, fabric soaking, boiling, drying, washing, and printing. 
  • Bagh prints are made by hand applying natural and vegetable-based dyes using carved wood relief blocks.
  • Red and black dyes are most common, but indigo, mustard, and khaki dyes are also used.

questions.question: 'Tholu Bommalatta’, a shadow puppet theatre tradition, belongs to the state of:
questions.questionHtml: 'Tholu Bommalatta’, a shadow puppet theatre tradition, belongs to the state of:
questions.solution: Tholu Bommalata is the shadow puppet theatre tradition of Andhra Pradesh. It involves performances using leather puppets and often narrates stories from Hindu epics like Ramayana and Mahabharata, showcasing a rich cultural heritage.

questions.question: Raja Ravi Varma, considered as one of the greatest painters of India, hailed from which of these states?
questions.questionHtml: Raja Ravi Varma, considered as one of the greatest painters of India, hailed from which of these states?
questions.solution: Raja Ravi Varma, one of India's greatest painters, hailed from Kerala and was honored with the Kaisar-i-Hind Gold Medal. Associated with Travancore's royal family, his famous works include "Arjuna and Subhadra," "Shakuntala," and "Mohini playing with a ball," showcasing his contributions to Indian art and culture.

questions.question: ‘Ankiya Nats’ are one-act plays distinct to the culture of ______.
questions.questionHtml: ‘Ankiya Nats’ are one-act plays distinct to the culture of ______.
questions.solution: Ankiya Nats are one-act plays unique to the cultural heritage of Assam. They were introduced by Srimanta Sankardeva, blending elements of dance, drama, and ballads, forming a significant aspect of Assam's artistic traditions.

questions.question: To which of the following states do 'Kajali Paintings’, in which no brush is used, traditionally belong?
questions.questionHtml: To which of the following states do 'Kajali Paintings’, in which no brush is used, traditionally belong?
questions.solution: Kajali Paintings, traditional to Rajasthan, use no brushes, relying on hand and cloth for application. Originating in eastern Rajasthan, this art uses carbon black from burning oil lamps, spread on surfaces with paper. The term 'Kajali' stems from 'kajal' (carbon black), and additional colors enhance its unique aesthetic.

questions.question: Charupallam, ‘the village of the incline’ is located near which temple?
questions.questionHtml: Charupallam, ‘the village of the incline’ is located near which temple?
questions.solution: The village of Charupallam is located near the Rajarajeshwara Temple in Thanjavur. This temple is known for its tallest shikhara and the architects built an inclined path to the top of the temple to place the 90 tonne stone for the top of the shikhara. The path started more than 4km away and was dismantled after the construction of the temple.

questions.question: Who painted the painting 'My Mother'?
questions.questionHtml: Who painted the painting 'My Mother'?
questions.solution: The painting 'My Mother' was painted by Abanindranath Tagore in 1912-13. It is a miniature painting decorated with an ornamental border. It was painted by Abanindranath Tagore after the death of his mother. He is the founder of Indian Society of Oriental Art.

questions.question: Temple for Goddess Nishumbhasudini was built by __________.
questions.questionHtml: Temple for Goddess Nishumbhasudini was built by __________.
questions.solution: The question focuses on the builder of the Nishumbhasudini Devi temple, attributed to the Chola dynasty. Vijayalaya Chola founded the dynasty, built the temple, and established Tanjore as the capital. Prominent Chola rulers like Rajendra I expanded the empire significantly. Chola governance included structured taxation, and their contributions to temple architecture were remarkable.
